messages.author: 3b35c2270d5c2281
messages.subject: Annotations of reference alignment
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering if there is a way to access the annotations DArT gives for the reference alignment? I have a set of outlier SNPs (from RDA and LFMM analyses) and want to find out which gene and function (in the LOCxxxx format) the corresponding outlier Allele ID is.

The format of the allele IDs (e.g. 82202452-33-A/G) from DArT does not corresponds to the names of the locus of the aligned reference genome of my samples (e.g. LOCxxxxx). 

Best,

Cilla

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Annotations of reference alignment
parts:
Hi Cilla,

Could you please expand on how/where you got the names of the locus of the aligned reference genome of your samples (e.g. LOCxxxxx)? 

One way to do it is that once you identify the SNPs, you are interested in, you "blast" (https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Blast.cgi) the Trimmed sequences of those SNPs. If you have DArT data and read it to dartR, you can find these trimmed sequences in the slot your_genlight$other$loc.metrics$TrimmedSequence. 

Once you identified the location of the SNPs by blasting them, you can start looking for the genes, proteins, etc, involving those SNPs by searching them in the many biological databases out there. Please look at the following link for a list of these databases. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_biological_databases 

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: Annotations of reference alignment
parts:
Hi Luis,

I did not get the locus names but rather its those names I want. I have blasted the trimmedrefsequences for the specific outlier loci but I only get hits for the whole refseq (e.g. Bombus terrestris genome assembly, chromosome 7, sequence ID:OU342927.1). I can search for the sequence ID in NCBI gene but then I get all genes on chr 7 and not the gene, exon etc of the trimmedrefsequences I originally entered. If I click on a Gene ID (LOCxxxx) then I can see the location of that gene on chr 7 (e.g. NC_015768.1 (5534828..5538242, complement), but its quite tedious going through all ~900 genes to find the right position....AND they have updated the ref genome for my study species so the position visible for each gene corresponds to the new ref genome and not the old version that DArT aligned my samples too, making it even harder to find the right position. Sorry this is abit outside of dartR problems....

Cilla
